newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine AvtoZAZ car deal with GM, Daewoo stalled.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine AvtoZAZ car deal with GM, Daewoo stalled.

text.p: A car-making joint venture between Ukraine's AvtoZAZ, General Motors of the U.S. and Daewoo Group of South Korea is in limbo until Ukraine passes two laws enabling the deal, AvtoZAZ officials said on Tuesday.

The deal announced in May has yet to be signed by the U.S. and South Korean carmakers, who are waiting for parliament to approve a law writing off debts of Ukraine's sole car maker and a second law guaranteeing tax breaks for the venture.

AvtoZAZ chief executive Alexander Sotnikov, asked if GM and Daewoo had given his company a final deadline to seal the deal which he pegged at $1.2 billion, replied, "I won't ask them and I hope it won't get to that moment."
Parliament, partly responsible for a nearly six-month delay in the 1997 budget finally passed on June 27, has voted to begin its summer break on July 18.
According to documents prepared by AvtoZAZ, the joint venture would involve upgrading the factory in the eastern city of Zaporizhya and boosting annual production eventually to 250-300,000 vehicles.
Direct investments from Daewoo would total $150 million followed by loans from both manufacturers, Sotnikov added.
"The risk is being taken by Daewoo and GM," he said.
Vehicle importers in Ukraine complaining of impending competition have been lobbying against the laws favouring AvtoZAZ.
Parliament is also considering a tax of about 60 percent on vehicle imports.

Sotnikov said if the deal went ahead AvtoZAZ would employ 20,000 people and produce a modernised version of its traditional Tavria and Dana vehicles, along with 45-75,000 GM cars and 150,000 Daewoo cars over a period of 10 years.
"Fifty percent of what's produced will be for export," Sotnikov said, adding the factory would also make car parts for export to neighbouring countries, and upgraded Daewoo engines.

AvtoZAZ has an annual capacity of 150,000 small and medium-sized cars, but production fell to only 6,881 cars last year from 130,000 cars in 1992 -- a year after Ukraine achieved independence from the Soviet Union.
